Compliance depends on the controller's operational procedure for fulfilling valid requests without undue delay across databases, uploaded files, generated order documents, logs, backups and recipients, and on applicable Article 17(3) retention exceptions. The repository cannot establish those procedures or their execution.

External destinations and personal-data flows are identifiable, but the repository cannot establish the deployed receiving legal entities, processing and onward-transfer countries, or a valid adequacy decision or Article 46 safeguard covering each transfer. Consequently, unknown third_country and adequacy_or_safeguards facts are omitted rather than asserted false. Determine the deployment's actual Google, social-sharing, blockchain/RPC, CloudWatch, webhook, notification, external-image and LLM recipients; whether transfers leave the EEA; and the applicable adequacy coverage or contractual/other safeguards. The LLM default is local (config/default.yml:22), and the configurable webhook and cloud deployment need not be used. Absence of transfer contracts in source code alone is not evidence of an unlawful transfer.

verdicts.deciding: The implemented request handler at routes/dataErasure.ts:83 only inserts deletionRequested=true and clears a cookie at routes/dataErasure.ts:88. It does not erase the account or associated personal data. User deletion is soft deletion because models/user.ts:120 enables paranoid mode. Compliance therefore depends on a controller-operated process outside the repository that actually erases eligible personal data, associated records, exported files, logs and downstream copies without undue delay, while handling Article 17(3) exceptions. Article 17 does not require an automated self-service deletion endpoint. The system.account_erasure=false fact describes the implemented application behavior, not proof that no external erasure process exists.

Actual recipients, processing locations, controller establishment and applicable transfer instruments are not established by source code. Google OAuth calls at frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68 and frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:173, Google Fonts at frontend/src/index.html:13, wallet/RPC integrations, optional webhooks at lib/webhook.ts:18 and the configurable LLM endpoint at routes/chat.ts:204 can disclose personal data. The LLM defaults to localhost at config/default.yml:22 and must not be assumed to be an overseas provider. Compliance requires the deployed transfer inventory, recipient legal entities and locations, and evidence of an applicable adequacy decision or Article 46 safeguards with enforceable rights and effective remedies. Transfer facts third_country and adequacy_or_safeguards are omitted rather than falsely treating unknown geography or missing contractual evidence as false.
